title: Project & Product Management: decide, plan, deliver, measure
intro: A PM keeps three things honest: what is worth building (value), when it will be done (schedule), and what it costs (budget), while managing risk and measuring whether the product works.
outcome: A prioritised backlog, a sprint plan, a schedule with a critical path, budget tracking with earned value, a risk register, and OKRs.

steps.title: Set the goal as OKRs
steps.what: An Objective is the outcome you want; Key Results are the measurable proof.
how: Open OKRs and add an objective with 2 to 4 key results.
Each KR has a start, a target and a current value.
KRs measure outcomes, not tasks.

steps.title: Build the backlog
steps.what: List the work as items: epic, story, task, bug, milestone.
how: Open the Board and add items with a clear title and owner.
Add points (effort) as a rough size.
Load the example project in Practice to see a complete one.
steps.ask: Break this goal into backlog items.

steps.title: Prioritise by value
steps.what: Rank by value per effort, not by who shouts loudest.
how: For each item enter reach, impact, confidence (0 to 1) and effort for RICE.
Or value, time criticality, risk reduction and points for WSJF.
Tag Must/Should/Could/Won't; Musts should stay near 60% of points.
steps.ask: Which of my items should I do first and why?

steps.title: Plan the schedule and find the critical path
how: Give items a start date, duration (days) and dependencies (ids).
Open Schedule: items with zero float are critical.
To finish sooner, shorten a critical item, not a slack one.
steps.done_when: You can name the critical path.
steps.ask: What is on my critical path and what would shorten it?

steps.title: Plan a sprint
steps.what: A sprint is a fixed time-box with a goal.
how: Add a sprint (2 weeks is common) with a goal.
Assign items to it when you add or edit them.
Do not commit more than your velocity.
steps.done_when: A sprint has a goal and assigned items.
mistakes: Committing to 30 points when velocity is 13.
steps.ask: How much should I commit to this sprint?

steps.title: Run the work and watch flow
steps.what: Move cards across the board and watch cycle time and WIP.
how: Move items from todo to doing to done on the Board.
Open Flow: cycle time, throughput, cumulative flow, Little's law.
If WIP is above what Little's law expects, stop starting and start finishing.
steps.done_when: You know your median cycle time and WIP.
steps.ask: Is my work in progress too high?

steps.title: Track budget with earned value
steps.what: Planned value, earned value and actual cost tell you if you are on track.
how: Enter planned and actual cost on items, or log your hours in the Time tab with an hourly rate: logged hours then replace the typed actual cost.
Open Earned value: CPI under 1 means over budget; SPI under 1 means behind.
Read EAC for the likely final cost.
steps.done_when: You can say whether you are over budget and behind.
mistakes: Planned cost missing on most items.
steps.ask: Explain my CPI and SPI in plain words.

steps.title: Manage risks
steps.what: A risk is a possible problem: probability times impact is its expected cost.
how: Open Risks and add each risk with probability (0 to 1) and cost.
Write a mitigation and an owner.
Use total exposure as a starting contingency reserve.
steps.ask: What risks am I probably missing?

steps.title: Measure the product
steps.what: Is anyone using it, and do they come back?
how: Open Product analytics: stickiness (DAU/MAU), status funnel, retention cohorts.
Entities stand in for accounts; records for activity.
mistakes: Reading a few rows as a trend.
steps.ask: What does my retention table say about the product?

steps.title: Review and adjust
steps.what: Use the numbers in the retro.
how: Check velocity trend, forecast, and risks.
Decide one thing to change next sprint.
steps.done_when: You wrote one change for next sprint.
steps.ask: Run a retrospective on my last sprint.
